title: Nominal/effective rate conversion declares compounding frequency
question: Applying a scalar Rate to Money is not nominal/effective interest conversion.

evidence.title: Nominal/effective conversion requires compounding context
explanation: Nominal/effective conversion explicitly rejects nonpositive compounding frequency and applies reciprocal power expressions using decimal-scalar rate units.
The two function bodies establish selected algebra and the frequency guard, not APR disclosure or exact-decimal financial arithmetic.

numPeriods>0, finite real-domain rate inputs; fractional powers of negative bases remain outside a demonstrated valid domain. The same nominal rate with different frequencies gives a different effective rate; no date basis, fees or annual disclosure convention follows from that formula. No upstream execution. The cited source branches and expressions were read; floating accuracy, actual resolved dependency versions and economic correctness are not certified. Prior R1-M1 dependency contracts are reused only within their recorded bounds. This behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core.
